A 5lb penalty for the four-year-old's latest triumph is unlikely to prevent another bold bid and a hat-trick may beckon. selections.comment: The in form AMBER HONEY is best placed to land a weak affair. She has shown a little impropvement since fitted with blinkers and arives on the back of a good second back over this trip on turf last time. Earlier in the year she was placed over course and distance and she has every chance if getting a decent pace to aim at. Raavi, the only other in the field to arrive in good form, looks the biggest threat having been eased a couple of pounds by the assessor despite a close-up third of seven last time. He's yet to try Polytrack but his only win came on the AW, on Tapeta at Wolverhampton. All his worthwhile form is over 6f but it's well worth another try at this trip (something amiss only try) and he's entitled to go close. Unknown Journey has form claims but is yet to convicne at the trip and looks to need further so the steadily progressive Atmosphere is next on the shortlist. He begins his handicap career stepping up from 6f (all three runs), which should suit well, and has shown a bit more with each run so far. An opening mark of 60 looks workable and he can land some of the spoils

selections.comment: MAHRA'S LOVE has a good opportunity to open her account on fifth time of asking. She went well on handicap debut when placed despite not getting the best of trips last time and she can take a step forward on her second try on Polytrack having gone well here on career debut when beaten less than 2.5l over an inadequate looking 6f. Maids Head could be dangerous seeking a double under similar conditions (won on Chelmsford's Poltrack surface last time over this trip) but takes a step up in class off a rise so Stella Hogan and Marchetti are feared more. The former has a fine course record with three of her four career wins coming here over 7f and a mile and arrives in fine fettle with a close-up fourth backing up a win prior. She's entitled to bang there again and can give the selection most to do. Marchetti has decent each way prospects if able to build on a fairly encouraging return to action after five months off when 5th of 12 on turf. The AW suits better and she's well suited to this track in particular with multiple placed efforts as well as a course and distance win, one of only two career wins

Tom Ward's gelding should be able to build on a promising 4th of 11 on debut at Leicester on fast ground if handling the switch to Polytrack. Galileo Island was a head in front of the selection at Leicester, but that was his second run and while it should be relatively tight between the two again Marco Botti's colt had an experience edge then and will find it tougher to keep the selection at bay today. He's still the main danger ahead of Rajak and a couple of interesting newcomers, Maskatto and Enhancer. Andrew Balding's debutant, Maskatto, is feared most of the trio given the yard is firing at a rate of nearly 25% with their juveniles this term

selections.comment: An open affair with nothing standing out and a few with something to porve but lurking on dangerous marks if rediscovering their best. UMBRIA looks the most solid choice even if she has to leave her latest effort well behind when switched back to the turf but she won over course and distance three runs back in November and was beaten under a length when sent off favourite here on her penultimate run. She can bounce back and go close. Trojan Storm went pretty well here upped to this level last time having won a class 5 event prior at Wolverhampton and given that came off a break should strip a touch fitter and on pnly his 8th start has scope for a bit of improvement yet. He should go well. Crystal Mariner, another who needs to bounce back, is feared back over conditions that suit well and looks to have found his level but Don Simon looks next best having knocked on the door twice on the AW before a slightly below par effort on turf last time

He's going the right way and may find a little more to land the top spot again. The Colorist is interesting but could be found out by the trip, so Autumn's Breeze merits a chance to deliver for each way backers having made an encouraging season comeback last time here over 1m4f and shapes as if stamina is her forte and could take a step forward upped to this 2m

He finished runner up that day despite being ridden overly aggressively and should like the quicker surface here. Recent point winner Emberscombe could also go well at big odds as she looks well treated on her hunter chase form and will appreciate this longer trip. Micronormous could do with some rain but isn't ruled out if it comes having dropped a fair way in the weights.

He lurks on a very dangerous mark on his flat form much like Init Together who split a pair of in form rivals over C&D last time and should remain competitive. He may have the beating of the consistent Brindley on collateral form but that rival should remain competitive as well.

selections.comment: ALRIGHT DAI was foiled in his hat trick bid in the spring but still ran well shaping as if this longer trip and stiffer track could bring about further improvement. He did look lazy that day but finished well suggesting that he could still be ahead of his current mark. Last year's winner Mactavish is respected off a 3lb higher mark as he was in good form until going off too quickly last time. Of those at likely bigger prices Mr Yeats is also feare having slipped to a good mark and he isn't fully exposed for this yard. He again raced lazily last time suggesting that this trip is on the sharp side but if the leaders get racing early he will be finishing strongly.

She has looked a touch unlucky not to add to her spring AW victory recently but should remain competitive while the inconsistent American In Paris also holds each way claims if turned out quickly.

selections.comment: A pair of standouts here in BARNAVARA and Faiyum. The latter is unbeaten in her short career and ought to relish this step up in trip so is feared considerably but the former sets the standard on form. Not only was she a Listed winner last time over 1m but previously she got within a neck of the future Coronation Stakes winner in the Athasi Stakes suggesting that if she sees out this longer trip she will be tough to beat. And So To Bed got close to the Oaks runner up at Group level last year and can fight for a place behind the selection.
